subject: c-fo-act
title: C.FO.ACT.------SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in NYM-30, closing the section's main argument. C-FO-ACT (composite focused activism) is crossed with SOC-RT (social reality), the structural pairing that the New York Movement section has been building toward — what does post-Ayler composite focused activism do to social reality, given everything the section has argued about isolation, gradualism, journalism dynamics, and the political-policy capture of reality options? SOC-RT → C-FO-ACT (the crossing). DEC (decentralization) → SOC-RT and ALT-F (alternative functionalism) → SOC-RT — meaning social reality is fed by both decentralization and alternative functionalism. C-FO-ACT → TRS (transition); CULT-INFO-B (culture information basis) → DYM-F (dynamic functionalism); TRS → DYM-F. POL-DYM (political dynamics) → TRS; LK-IMP (linkage implications) → POL-DYM. Structural argument: composite focused activism is downstream of social reality (which is itself fed by decentralization and alternative functionalism — the structural prerequisites the section identified as necessary). The productive output runs C-FO-ACT → transition → dynamic functionalism, with culture-information-basis as a parallel feed into dynamic functionalism (meaning dynamic functionalism is over-determined upstream). Linkage implications produces political dynamics, which produces transition. The diagram closes the section by structurally acknowledging that the post-Ayler movement's productive output (dynamic functionalism via transition) requires *both* decentralization-grounded social reality *and* the linkage-implications → political-dynamics chain. The political dynamics chain is not the enemy — it is one of the necessary feeds into transition, alongside the composite focused activism the New York School embodied.
